title: Tesla's China-Made Vehicle Sales Rise 10.3% in October
detail:
Tesla's China-Made Vehicle Sales Rise 10.3% in October
Faizan Farooque
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 1:22 PM EST 2 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Although the numbers demonstrate why it is still challenging to evaluate Tesla's (TSLA, Financials) competitive position in China, the company reported another month of year-over-year growth from its Shanghai factory in October.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The China Passenger Car Association reports that Tesla sold 67,829 Model 3 and Model Y cars built in China during the month, a 10.3% increase over the same period last year.

That was an improvement over the 5% increase in September and the 12th consecutive month of annual growth.

Nevertheless, October's volume was 28.9% less than September's 95,366 vehicles, which was the factory's best month in 2026.

The Shanghai figures include exports as well as cars sold to Chinese consumers, which is a crucial distinction.

Tesla delivered 381,088 cars domestically in the first nine months of 2026, a decrease of 11.9% from the same period the previous year.

In contrast, exports more than doubled to 361,972 automobiles.

This indicates that foreign markets, rather than increased demand within China, have contributed significantly to Shanghai's growth.

Improved registrations in a number of European nations and a growing presence in South Korea, which accounted for roughly one-fifth of Shanghai exports during the first nine months, have benefited the factory.

Tesla is under increasing pressure to compete with domestic manufacturers on pricing, product features, and model selection as China's larger electric vehicle market continues to grow.

According to preliminary industry data, new-energy passenger car wholesale sales nationwide reached about 1.8 million in October, up 12% from the same month the previous year.

As a result, Tesla's 10.3% growth lagged behind the overall market, though the numbers do not show a shift in its domestic market share.

The release of October's domestic delivery and export breakdown, which will give a clearer picture of whether Tesla is gaining ground with Chinese consumers, is the next catalyst.

Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Block Their Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Venue

Two of Elon Musk's companies are now keeping their shares off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Tesla and SpaceX are among six new objecting issuers listed in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Monday. Amazon, Netflix, Lam Research, and SoFi Technologies are the others. The additions bring the total to 56 companies.

The list stood at 50 in the venue's Oct. 30 notice, when Nvidia, Costco, and Nike led the biggest batch yet. That followed 38 on Oct. 28, after Walmart joined, and nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

The new names deepen the roster of megacap holdouts. Amazon, Tesla, and Netflix join Microsoft, Alphabet, and Nvidia, while SoFi, a fintech company that offers crypto trading, adds a company with its own stake in digital assets. SpaceX, which trades under the ticker SPCX, rounds out the batch.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.

If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. The objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

To trade, users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable "soulbound" token that the venue's smart contracts verify before every transaction.

Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Apple is now one of the few megacap names still missing from the list. And while objections bar OKXICE from listing third-party tokenized versions of a company's stock, they don't close every door.

The notice says the venue can also list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, though it doesn't identify any, and that tokenized stocks it offers aren't restricted to trading on OKXICE alone.

title: CFTC Greenlights Perpetual Futures on U.S. Stocks
detail:
CFTC Greenlights Perpetual Futures on U.S. Stocks
William M. Peaster

AAPL

TSLA
COIN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

CFTC Chair Mike Selig announced this morning that perpetual futures on individual U.S. equities can begin trading on CFTC-registered exchanges for the first time. The products are classified as security futures, which puts them under both CFTC and SEC oversight.

What's the Scoop?

The ruling: The contracts were "deemed approved" under Commission Regulation 40.3, meaning the review window closed without objection. Only venues that are both CFTC-designated contract markets and SEC notice-registered for security futures can list them. The statement names no exchanges and no tickers.

Who's in line: Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives, and Bitnomial (Kraken's parent, Payward) all filed perp rules on Sept. 18th. Kalshi's filing covers up to 58 contracts on large caps including Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla; Bitnomial's starter list is ten names. Coinbase Vice Chairman Ryan VanGrack said the exchange is "getting equity perps ready for U.S. customers." No venue has posted a launch date.

Not the offshore product: The filed contracts run Sunday evening to Friday afternoon ET, not 24/7, with margin floors around 15%, or roughly 6.5x leverage. Offshore venues go much higher, and nothing here opens Hyperliquid's existing stock perps to Americans. Even still, Hyperliquid Strategies CEO David Schamis called this new classification "a real step toward bringing Hyperliquid onshore."

The pushback: SIFMA asked regulators yesterday to pause and take public comment first, Better Markets called the products a gambling tool in disguise, and CME is still suing the CFTC on the theory that perps are swaps, not futures.

Chinese tape maker Crown New Materials Technology surged as much as 787% in its market debut Tuesday, creating two billionaires on paper just as Beijing reportedly moved to restrict new IPO filings amid a stock-market slump.

Shares reached 150.58 yuan from their 16.98-yuan IPO price, triggering two trading halts. They closed at 84.55 yuan, still up nearly 398%.

A Tape Maker Creates Two Billionaires

Crown makes industrial adhesives and protective films used in supply chains serving Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA).

The explosive gains turned Crown's chairman, Mai Michael, a former elementary-school teacher, and his sister, Mai Huixia, into billionaires, with estimated fortunes of $2.5 billion and $2 billion, respectively.

But Crown's earnings are moving the other way. Revenue rose 11.75% in the first nine months of 2026 while net profit fell 7.89%, according to a company filing.

Ahead of its debut, Crown warned investors against "blindly following the crowd" in speculation on newly listed shares.

Only 9.4% of Crown's shares were available to trade, leaving investors competing for limited supply. Shen Meng, managing director of Beijing-based investment bank Chanson & Co., told Forbes that conservative IPO pricing and strong investor demand help explain the extraordinary gains.

China's IPO Frenzy Meets a Market Slump

Crown's rally is part of a much bigger IPO frenzy. New listings in Shanghai and Shenzhen gained an average 234% on their first trading day in September, according to Chinese brokerage Guotai Haitong Securities.

But established stocks have been struggling. The CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October, while the technology-heavy STAR 50 plunged about 40% in less than four months, wiping out roughly $480 billion, Reuters reported.

The contrast helps explain Beijing's latest intervention: while investors are piling into new listings, regulators are trying to support shares already on the market.

Beijing Moves to Restrict New IPOs

China's securities regulator told investment banks Monday to stop submitting new IPO applications, while allowing those already in the pipeline to proceed, the Wall Street Journal reported.

By limiting the supply of new shares, Beijing hopes to support prices of existing stocks. The restrictions could remain until the market recovers, according to the Financial Times.

That could create problems for companies planning to go public, including AI developer DeepSeek, which has reportedly hired CITIC Securities to prepare a listing.

Tesla's (TSLA) China-made electric vehicle sales extended their annual growth streak to 12 consecutive months in October, as the EV maker recorded a sharp recovery across several European markets despite growing competition from Chinese automakers.

TSLA shares edged 1% higher in pre-market trading on Tuesday.

Tesla's Shanghai-Made EV Sales Jump 10%

According to a report by CNEVPost on Tuesday, Tesla sold 67,829 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles manufactured at its Shanghai facility in October, up 10.3% year over year.

However, wholesale sales, which include domestic deliveries and exports, fell 28.9% sequentially, reaching their lowest level since February. Despite the sequential decline, Tesla's China-made vehicle sales rose 21.4% year over year to 810,889 units during the first 10 months of 2026.

Tesla Stages Strong European Recovery

Meanwhile, Tesla continued its European recovery, with October vehicle registrations surging 248% in Sweden, 131% in Norway and 34% in Denmark, according to Reuters. Registrations also climbed 271% in Spain, 186% in Portugal and 94% in Italy.

The rebound was supported by higher fuel prices, government incentives and rising EV demand, the report read.

While Tesla emerged as Norway's top-selling brand in October, competition remained intense in Denmark, where it was outperformed by Chinese rivals BYD, Leapmotor, Xpeng and MG.

Why Is Tesla's Shanghai Factory In Focus?

Tesla's Shanghai factory has an installed annual production capacity exceeding 950,000 vehicles, making it one of the company's most important manufacturing and export hubs. However, the facility is in the spotlight due to potential complications in the merger between Tesla and SpaceX (SPCX).

Last week, Bank of America flagged China as the biggest regulatory risk to the proposed combination, as the merger would bring Tesla's Shanghai operations under the ownership of a major U.S. defense contractor.

The brokerage warned that national security concerns could complicate Chinese regulatory approval. Former Tesla board member Steve Westly had also highlighted similar concerns over the merger recently.
